Text: Humana is positioned for a significant earnings recovery following improvements in its 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, according to Evercore analyst Elizabeth Anderson. Humana recorded broad improvements across multiple contracts, including its key H5216 contract, which achieved 4-star summary ratings for both Medicare Part C and Part D. Of 13 contracts, four gained a star while one lost a star. Text: $UNH Part 1 Following UnitedHealth Group’s (UNH) third quarter 2026 earnings conference call, the remaining capacity under their share repurchase program is tracked across two metrics: management's annual dollar guidance and the board's authorized share facility. 1. In Dollars (Annual Capital Allocation Target) Year-to-Date Repurchased: Through the end of Q3 2026, UnitedHealth repurchased $5.0 billion of its common stock. Full-Year Target: Management previously raised its 2026 full-year repurchase target to "at least $5.0 billion" (up from an initial $2.5 billion). Remaining for 2026: Because UNH reached the $5.0 billion mark by the end of Q3, there is no formal remaining dollar commitment left on their minimum target for the year. Management noted that fourth-quarter capital deployment remains balanced against their debt-to-capital ratio goal, which stood at 41.7% at the end of Q3 with a year-end target approaching 40.0%.

Author: newtwo99
Text: $UNH Part 2 2. In Shares (Board Authorized Facility) UnitedHealth Group’s Board of Directors authorizes repurchases on a share-count basis rather than a fixed dollar ceiling, with no fixed expiration date: June 30, 2026 Balance: As of the close of Q2 2026, 10.6 million shares remained authorized under the board-approved repurchase program (down from 19.3 million at the end of Q1 2026). Q3 2026 Activity: UnitedHealth deployed approximately $1.0 billion into share buybacks during Q3 (advancing from $4.0 billion at Q2 to $5.0 billion year-to-date). At UNH’s average Q3 trading range (~$355–$375 per share), this accounted for roughly 2.7 to 2.8 million shares retired. Estimated Remaining Facility: Heading into Q4 2026, an estimated ~7.8 to 8.0 million shares remain authorized under the existing facility, pending the final Item 703 table in the upcoming Q3 Form 10-Q filing

Text: Big pharmaceutical stocks are trading at or near all-time highs as investors shift away from volatile technology shares and seek more defensive investments amid the ongoing tech selloff. These companies are also working to extend patent protection for their best-selling medicines, helping sustain revenue and support long-term growth. Thursday’s gains reflected the sector’s strength: Eli Lilly rose 4.78%, AbbVie gained 1.13% and Gilead Sciences advanced 3.29%. Amgen climbed 3.03% and UnitedHealth Group increased 3.71%, while the healthcare sector ETF XLV gained 2.28% and the biotech ETF XBI rose 1.89%. Merck was a notable exception, slipping 0.21%.
